newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's main crude ports remain closed - officials.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's main crude ports remain closed - officials.

text.p: Mexico's three principal crude oil shipping ports and 20 terminals remained closed on Tuesday because of strong winds, officials from the port authority and the Communications and Transport Ministry said.
A storm front passing over the Yucatan peninsula and Gulf of Mexico since Monday, continued whipping up winds of more than 50 miles (80 kilometers) per hour.
Poor weather conditions shut Mexico's three main crude ports - Dos Bocas in Tabasco state, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state and Pajaritos in Veracruz state.
The ministry said 20 terminals in the states of Tamaulipas, Veracruz, Tabasco, Campeche and Yucatan remain closed because of dangerously high waves.
Winds appeared to be dying down, according to the ministry, and some ports could reopen later Tuesday.
